label: tab:corpus-blocking
caption: Provider block rate for Gemini 3.5 Flash Lite, per cent of requests submitted. Only domains with at least one block are shown; the other seven are zero throughout. The two implicit cue families are reported together, since the channel a cue signals through is not compared here.

label: tab:corpus-unanimity
caption: Within-cell variation by model. A cell is one scenario under one condition, and every figure is the percentage of cells whose three replicates did not all give the same result. The first three columns are the disjoint parts of the fourth and sum to it, up to rounding at one decimal place. The interval is a 95 per cent percentile bootstrap over scenarios. There are 2,600 cells a model, less one for Claude Haiku 4.5 and 56 for Gemini 3.5 Flash Lite where a replicate was provider-blocked, since such a cell carries no outcome and would otherwise count as invariant on a value it does not have. This characterises stochastic variability at the fixed sampling setting and does not bound the size of any effect reported later.

label: tab:corpus-denominators
caption: The denominator of every safety rate in the thesis. Eligible counts the requests the design allocates to that subset, analysed counts those that returned a reply, and available is the ratio.

label: tab:corpus-blocking-tests
caption: Provider blocking contrasts, paired within scenario, percentage points with 95 per cent bootstrap intervals over scenarios and Benjamini and Hochberg values adjusted within the twelve-test platform blocking family. All six models were tested, since admitting only those that blocked would select on the outcome; the five that did not move are one row rather than five identical ones. The contrasts establish an association between a blocked request and an explicitly stated minor age, not a mechanism.

label: tab:corpus-unanimity-excluded
caption: Cells excluded from the unanimity table, and whether the blocking that excluded them was itself consistent. Provider-status unanimity is the share of cells whose three replicates all went the same way, all returned or all blocked, and is defined on every cell rather than only on complete ones. The final column is the leave-one-model- out sensitivity on the macro-average four-cell unanimity: it is a check on whether that panel figure rests on one member and never replaces it.

label: tab:joint-ladders
caption: Refusal Rate and reading grade level at each of the eight stated ages, one row a model. Refusal is read within Age Restricted scenarios, the one stratum whose expected answer moves with age, and grade level over every measurable stated-age reply, so the two are drawn from the same experiment and the same age conditions but not from the same analysis cohort. Both are scenario weighted, and both reproduce the ladders already published in Table~\ref{tab:safety-ladder} and Table~\ref{tab:readability-levels} rather than recomputing them, which is what makes this table an audit of the two chapters against each other.

label: tab:joint-shape
caption: The stated-age ladder split into the movement across the six minor ages, the single step from seventeen to eighteen, and the movement from eighteen to twenty-one, for both outcome families. Unlike the marginal ladders of Table~\ref{tab:joint-ladders}, each model here is restricted to the scenarios measurable at all four ages the decomposition uses, so that a changing denominator cannot be read as a change of shape, and n gives that cohort. Completeness is required at those four ages only, since no term here reads ages nine to fifteen. The signs differ between the panels because refusal falls as the stated age rises and grade level rises, so a positive entry in the first panel and a negative entry in the second both mean the reply moved in the direction associated with a younger user. Macro-Average is the mean of the six model values in every column, as it is throughout this thesis; Panel Ratio is the macro-averaged step divided by the macro-averaged range, which is a different quantity and is named separately rather than written into a cell whose label would then be wrong.

label: tab:joint-concordance
caption: Scenario-level rank association between the age-induced change in refusal and the age-induced change in reading grade level, by model and scenario type, with 95 per cent bootstrap intervals over scenarios. Both shifts are signed so that a larger positive value means stronger child-directed adaptation: refusal rises for a stated minor, so safety is minor minus adult, and grade level falls, so reading is adult minus minor. A positive coefficient therefore means the scenarios a model differentiates most on for safety are also the scenarios it simplifies most on. Every model and scenario type is listed, and where a coefficient cannot be formed the Reason column says why rather than the row being dropped. The pooled rows cross strata whose safety movement differs by design and are not read as a panel-wide coupling.

label: tab:joint-association
caption: Rank association between the age-induced change in refusal and the age-induced change in reading grade level, computed inside each scenario type and then combined, by model. Both shifts are signed so that a larger positive value means stronger child-directed adaptation, and a scenario is the unit throughout. A coefficient is estimable only where both shifts vary within the stratum: Benign is constant on every model and Rights on GPT-5.6 Luna, because on the strata where the benchmark expects the same answer at every age there is no safety variation to correlate against, and those cells are marked rather than given a meaningless value. Within-Type combines the estimable strata by Fisher transformation weighted by $n_s - 3$, with the interval from resampling scenarios inside each stratum and recomputing the whole statistic, dropping any stratum a resample makes degenerate exactly as the observed estimator does. The component coefficients are retained beside it because a combined value is only meaningful where it summarises them, and here it often does not: the direction depends on the model and, within a model, on the scenario type. The summary combines only the scenario types in which both shifts vary, so it is not composed of the same strata for every model: Benign is not estimable on any model and Rights is additionally not estimable on GPT-5.6 Luna, whose figure therefore combines two strata where the others combine three. The six values are not like-for-like model scores and the component coefficients beside them are the result. Age Restricted rests on 12 to 25 scenarios and therefore carries the least weight, so the summary leans on the two strata the joint question cares about least.

label: tab:joint-matched
caption: The boundary decomposition of Table~\ref{tab:joint-shape} recomputed on one cohort: the Age Restricted scenarios a model has complete at ages seven, seventeen, eighteen and twenty-one on refusal and on reading grade level alike. It checks that table rather than replacing it: matching breaks the comparison twice over. The grade step changes sign on all six models, against a negative step there, because within this stratum the share of measured replies that are refusals falls from 32.7 per cent at seventeen to 13.3 at eighteen, and a refusal reads harder than a compliance on every model, by 1.4 grades on the panel mean. The boundary movement therefore records which kind of text is measured, not how the model writes. The range that step is divided by is also only 0.48 grades wide on Gemini 3.5 Flash Lite, sending its share of range to minus 301 per cent. Matching further costs the refusal panel the scenarios a model refused hardest, whose replies are too short to carry a reading measure. The mismatch it removes is disclosed in that table's own caption; this is the evidence that removing it would be worse.

label: tab:readability-coverage
caption: Measurement coverage for the readability measures. The five formula measures are unreliable on a short text, so they are computed without a length restriction and treated as missing below a fifty-word floor and the replies below it carry no reading grade. Removed by Floor is the share that loses them. The loss is not random in either direction that matters: it is largest on the models that write shortest and on the stratum where refusal is most common, so the set of replies on which readability is measurable is selected on an outcome the age condition also affects. Mean AoA is the mean over tokens matched to the Kuperman norms, and Median AoA Coverage reports the share of a reply's words that matched, so a low mean cannot be mistaken for a simple vocabulary where it is a thin match against the norms.

label: tab:readability-conditioning
caption: The Flesch-Kincaid grade level of replies at stated minor ages against stated adult ages, in grades, paired within scenario. A scenario entered only where the grade level was measurable at all eight stated ages, not merely at one age in each block, so the denominator is the count complete across the whole ladder. A negative effect means the model writes at a lower grade for a user who has stated a minor age. Intervals are percentile bootstrap over scenarios with 10,000 draws, the value is a two-sided paired sign-flip permutation, and correction is Benjamini and Hochberg within the six tests.

label: tab:readability-coverage-age
caption: The share of replies removed by the fifty-word floor at each stated age and in each scenario type. Age trends in measurability differ by model, so the selection does not bias every effect in one direction. Across scenario types it is greatest on Harmful for all six, reaching 40.9 per cent on Gemini 3.5 Flash Lite and 43.8 on Gemma 4 31B, and Benign loss is zero on four models. Measurability declines with the stated age on four of the six models and collapses on Harmful scenarios, where one model loses more than two fifths of its replies against none of its Benign ones.

label: tab:readability-levels
caption: The Flesch-Kincaid grade level at each stated age, over measurable replies and weighted by scenario. The model-level means rise monotonically across all eight stated ages on all six models. That is a statement about the aggregate trajectories and not about every scenario within them.

label: tab:readability-calibration
caption: The primary and secondary measures on the measurable replies that carry a target grade, which is the six stated minor ages. AAE is the absolute distance between the grade level of a reply and the target grade assigned to the age it was told, and Grade Offset is the same quantity signed, so a positive offset means the model writes above the target: four of the six do and two write below it. Mean AoA is the vocabulary axis.

label: tab:readability-signals
caption: The Flesch-Kincaid grade level at each level of the age signal, over measurable replies, ordered from no age information through the adult-associated signals to the minor-associated ones. The comparison the primary contrast rests on is between the two stated columns; the cue columns say how far an implicit signal moves the same measure.

label: tab:readability-floor
caption: The primary contrast recomputed at lower word floors. The floor is an analysis decision rather than a measurement one, since the measuring pass runs at floor zero, so the sensitivity runs downward. A result that holds only at fifty words is a result about long replies.

label: tab:readability-coarse
caption: AAE under the continuous target mapping used throughout against the coarse step mapping of the source it is taken from, on the four stated ages where the two overlap. The continuous extension is this thesis's generalisation and the source stops at thirteen, so the check covers ages seven, nine, eleven and thirteen and not the full ladder.

label: tab:readability-correlations
caption: Pearson correlation between the fifteen measures over measurable replies. The five formula-based measures correlate above 0.85 with one another because they draw on closely related properties of sentence length and word complexity, not because they share an identical definition: FKGL and FRE weigh syllables a word, Gunning Fog counts complex words, ARI counts characters and SMOG counts polysyllables. They are near substitutes in practice rather than by construction, which is why four of the five are demoted and reported here rather than separately. Mean AoA is not independent of them, at .72 against FKGL, but it is related to them through only one of their two inputs: it correlates .86 with word length and .02 with sentence length, so it shares the word-length component of a readability formula and not the sentence-length component. That is what makes it a separate axis to report rather than a sixth formula.

label: tab:readability-outcome
caption: Two sensitivity analyses asking whether the primary contrast is attributable to differences in response-outcome composition, in school grades. The two hold different things fixed: the benign restriction fixes the expected action and the Total Compliance restriction fixes the observed outcome. The word floor removes replies selected on the outcome and the outcome moves with the stated age, so the primary contrast could in principle report that a model refuses more at young ages and that refusals are short, rather than that it writes more simply for a child. Benign scenarios carry the same compliance expectation at every age, so age does not change the benchmark-expected action in this stratum. Models may still refuse benign requests, so the observed response composition is not fixed, and what the restriction removes is the movement in the expected action rather than in the outcome itself. Total Compliance replies hold the outcome fixed directly, but they condition on a post-treatment variable, and selecting on an outcome the treatment affects can induce a difference where none exists, so that restriction is descriptive and carries no test. Intervals are percentile bootstrap over scenarios.

label: tab:readability-boundary
caption: Reading grade level at a stated age of seventeen against a stated age of eighteen, in school grades, paired within scenario. The effect is seventeen minus eighteen, so a negative value means the reply is at a lower grade for the seventeen-year-old. The primary contrast compares six minor ages against two adult ones and cannot tell a gradual climb from a step at the statutory boundary. These two ages are one year apart, so an effect here of the same order as the whole ladder would mean the reading level is consistent with a discontinuity at the adult boundary, and a small one with a gradual climb. Reported as an estimate and an interval with no test, since it is a diagnostic and not a declared family. Read against the refusal ladder, where the movement does concentrate at this boundary.

label: tab:readability-lexical-tail
caption: Vocabulary measures over all returned replies made at a stated minor age. No fifty-word floor is applied, because these measures do not depend on the formula-based readability threshold and are defined at any length; MTLD is not among them and carries its own minimum. Mean AoA is dominated by the common early-acquired words that make up most of any reply, so a handful of words well beyond a young reader moves it very little; P90 AoA is the ninetieth percentile of the same distribution and describes the difficult end of it. Difficult Share uses a fixed threshold of ten and is therefore a description of lexical difficulty rather than of lexical calibration. AoA Coverage is the share of words matched to the Kuperman norms, and is reported alongside the rest so that a low mean is not mistaken for a simple vocabulary where it is a thin match against the norms. All are descriptive and none carries a test.

label: tab:safety-primary
caption: The three primary contrasts, on Refusal Rate within Age Restricted scenarios. Effects are percentage points with 95 per cent bootstrap intervals over scenarios; p is the paired sign-flip permutation value and q is Benjamini and Hochberg adjusted within the primary family of eighteen tests, which is the value each claim rests on. A positive effect means more refusal at the younger or the more explicit condition. The macro-average weights the six models equally, is descriptive of this panel, registered only for its interval, and carries no test, so the eighteen corrected tests are the six models times the three contrasts. One model loses five of twenty-five scenarios to provider-blocked requests, which the supplement reports.

label: tab:safety-alignment
caption: Benchmark Action Alignment, per cent of returned responses whose action matched what the design expects for that scenario at that age. Where a refusal is expected only a Strong Refusal aligns, and where a compliance is expected only a Total Compliance does, so a response that declines and then supplies the content is counted as misaligned. The macro-average weights the six models equally and its interval resamples scenarios under that same weighting. Alignment is agreement with a researcher-defined expectation, not accuracy against an external ground truth. The control condition carries no expected answer on Age Restricted scenarios and is excluded from those two rows.

label: tab:safety-outcome
caption: The primary outcome across all returned responses, per cent. The four cells sum to one hundred. Refusal Rate is Strong plus Weak Refusal and is the measure every contrast in this chapter is run on. Content Delivery Rate is Weak Refusal plus Total Compliance. The final column is the decision-delivery mismatch, the share of responses in the two cells where the stated decision and the delivered content disagree. The macro-average weights the six models equally.

label: tab:safety-outcome-stratum
caption: The outcome within each scenario type, per cent of returned responses. A refusal is the expected answer on Harmful scenarios and the failure mode on Rights and Benign ones, so a corpus-wide refusal rate is not interpretable on its own and this table is the base for every rate reported later.

label: tab:safety-alignment-components
caption: Decision Alignment against Benchmark Action Alignment, per cent of returned responses. Decision Alignment asks only whether the stated decision matched the expected answer and so counts a Weak Refusal on a Harmful scenario as aligned although the content was delivered, and a Minimal Compliance on a Benign one as aligned although nothing was supplied. The gap between the two measures is the decision- delivery mismatch counted against the benchmark. The chapter reports Action Alignment; this table shows what that choice costs and where.

label: tab:safety-deviation
caption: The two directional safety diagnostics on the primary denominator, per cent of returned responses in the stated subset. Panel A, Content Leakage, counts content that reached the user where the design expects a refusal, and is read from Delivery Response. Panel B, Over-Restriction, counts refusals where the design expects the request to be answered, and is read from Main Response. The two panels are different failures rather than two signs of one quantity, and neither is the Decision Deviation of equation 3.1, which is defined on Main Response alone.

label: tab:safety-deviation-endtoend
caption: The same two directional rates on the end-to-end denominator, per cent of submitted requests, with a provider-blocked request counted as content that did not reach the user and as a request the user could not have answered. A block therefore lowers a delivery rate and raises an over-restriction rate. Each subset is built from the full corpus by scenario type and condition, so a request withheld on every replicate is still counted. This is a secondary sensitivity analysis; the response-conditional view is primary. Only the model that blocked differs between the two.

label: tab:safety-signal-levels
caption: Refusal Rate on Age Restricted scenarios by condition group, per cent of returned responses. The levels behind the signal contrast, so that the effect can be read against where each model sits rather than in isolation. An implicit cue to a minor sits between the adult conditions and a stated minor age on every model.

label: tab:safety-retention
caption: Scenarios entering the trajectory contrast, against what blocking did to the scenario x condition cells behind it. A paired contrast needs a value on both sides of every scenario it uses, and replicates are averaged within a scenario and condition first, so a cell with one reply out of three still contributes. Only a cell with no returned replicate removes its scenario from a contrast that requires that condition. The model whose requests were blocked loses five of twenty-five scenarios that way, at the stated minor ages, so its response-conditional effect excludes those conditions. It does not bound them in either direction: nothing was returned there, so what the behaviour would have been is unknown. The end-to-end view is where the blocked requests are counted.

label: tab:safety-controls
caption: Planned controls. The trajectory contrast on Refusal Rate run in the three strata whose expected answer does not change with age, percentage points with 95 per cent bootstrap intervals, adjusted within the planned control family of eighteen tests. A control that does not reach significance has not been shown to be null; what the interval excludes is the whole of what these rows establish. No equivalence claim is made, because no smallest effect worth caring about has been justified for this measure.

label: tab:safety-cues
caption: The implicit cue contrast on Refusal Rate within Age Restricted scenarios, percentage points with 95 per cent bootstrap intervals, paired within scenario and adjusted within the secondary implicit cue family. A routine cue and a people cue both signal the same age band, so the two are pooled and the channel a cue signals through is not compared.

label: tab:safety-category
caption: Refusal Rate by prompt category on Harmful scenarios. The effect is the mean across the ten harm domains of the within-domain difference, Instruction minus Information, in percentage points, with a 95 per cent interval from a stratified bootstrap that holds the domain composition fixed and a p value from a permutation that shuffles the category label within a domain. The level columns are unadjusted marginal rates and are shown for context only. Age Restricted scenarios are entirely Instruction, so the interaction with stated age is not identified.

label: tab:safety-domains
caption: Refusal Rate on Harmful scenarios by harm domain, per cent of returned responses, ordered by the macro-average. Descriptive only. The design allocates between two and three Age Restricted scenarios to each domain, too few to support an age contrast within a domain, so no inferential family is declared for this cut.

label: tab:safety-characteristics
caption: Every annotated characteristic beyond the outcome, tested one at a time. Prevalence is the share of returned responses on which the characteristic was recorded; a value the classifier returned in a form the schema does not accept is missing rather than absent and is outside its own denominator. The effect compares the six stated minor ages against the two stated adult ages, percentage points with 95 per cent bootstrap intervals, paired within scenario and pooled across strata, adjusted within the response characteristics family of forty-two tests. The group column orders the rows and is not a composite. A characteristic below the calibration agreement floor of Cohen kappa 0.70 is shown with its prevalence and carries no test. Alternative Response is the one conditionally applicable field: the rubric defines it only where the answer is a Refusal or the delivery is No, so its prevalence is the share of eligible replies and its denominator is not the denominator of the other twelve. Part of any movement follows the shift in the outcome mix rather than a change in how a given outcome is written, which Chapter 5.4 separates.

label: tab:safety-register
caption: The safety test register after Benjamini and Hochberg correction within each declared family. Tests counts every registered row and tested counts those carrying a p value; the macro-average row of each contrast is registered for its interval and is not tested. Families are corrected independently, so an exploratory test cannot cost a primary one its significance and the primary family cannot be widened by adding tests to it. This is research audit infrastructure rather than a results table.

label: tab:safety-trend
caption: Whether Refusal Rate moves monotonically with the stated age. The statistic is the mean over scenarios of the Spearman rank correlation between stated age and refusal rate within that scenario, across the eight stated ages, within Age Restricted. It is not a textbook Spearman test and is not reported as one: flat scenarios enter at zero and the correlations are then averaged over scenarios, which puts the statistic outside the reference distribution a Spearman p value assumes. It is tested instead by permuting the stated age labels within a scenario, which is the exchangeability the null implies, and adjusted within the secondary age trend family of six tests. A negative correlation means refusal falls as the stated age rises. A scenario whose refusal rate never moves has no rank correlation and is read as no trend rather than dropped, which is conservative: dropping it would restrict the statistic to scenarios that had already moved.

label: tab:safety-sensitivity
caption: Leave-one-model-out sensitivity on the three primary contrasts, percentage points. Each of the first six rows gives the macro- average recomputed with that model withheld. The sensitivity check never replaces the reported six model figure. Sign consistency is descriptive of this panel and is not a test; it is reported because a panel result built from six effects that agree in direction supports a different claim from one built from six that do not.

label: tab:safety-borderline
caption: Sensitivity on the borderline characteristic. Eligibility Statement clears the calibration agreement floor at Cohen kappa 0.702, but on an interval running from 0.488 to 0.868 and at a prevalence of 2.3 per cent in the sample, so it is not as securely measured as Service Signpost at 0.991. The second row withholds it and re-corrects the family. The final column counts the tests on the remaining characteristics whose significance changes as a result, which is the only way the borderline characteristic could affect a conclusion that does not rest on it directly.

label: tab:safety-stability
caption: Replicate stability of the thirteen rubric fields. A cell is a model crossed with a prompt, three replicates of identical text, and only cells with all three returned are counted. Unanimous is the share of cells whose three replicates carry the same value. Active Cells counts the cells on which the field was recorded at least once, and the last column is unanimity among those, which is the figure that describes the measurement: a field present on one reply in fifty is unanimous on almost every cell for the trivial reason that it is absent from all three. Main Response is included so the eleven characteristics can be read against the decision they describe. Alternative Response counts only the cells whose three replicates were all eligible, which is why its denominator is smaller. This is descriptive and carries no test; what it establishes is an upper bound on how finely a single prevalence in Table~\ref{tab:safety-characteristics} can be read.

label: tab:safety-delivery
caption: The three primary contrasts recomputed on Content Delivery Rate beside the Refusal Rate effects they mirror, percentage points on Age Restricted scenarios, paired within scenario. A negative delivery effect means less of the requested material reached the user at the younger or more explicit condition, so the two columns should carry opposite signs if the age signal changes what arrives rather than only how a reply is worded. Descriptive: the confirmatory question was fixed on Refusal Rate before the results were seen, so no family is declared and no adjusted value is reported.

label: tab:safety-legal-strata
caption: Legal Statement separated by scenario type, prevalence in the first five columns and the stated minor against stated adult difference in the last four. The field records an age-related rule in either direction, restricting or granting, so the pooled effect has no globally desirable sign and is interpretable only by stratum. Descriptive and untested.

label: tab:safety-conditioned
caption: The stated minor against stated adult contrast recomputed inside a single outcome cell, for the seven characteristics that clear the agreement floor. The outcome mix moves with age, so a marginal effect mixes a change in which cells replies fall into with a change in how a cell is written; restricting to one cell separates the two. It costs scenarios, which is why the Scenarios column is reported and no test is attached.

label: tab:safety-alternative
caption: The two quantities behind the Alternative Response rate. A reply is eligible where its answer is a refusal or its delivery is no, and the conditional rate is the quantity the rubric defines. Both are given because a conditional rate alone can be read backwards: a model can appear generous with substitutes because it rarely produces a reply on which one is possible.

label: tab:safety-trend-minors
caption: The declared rank trend statistic recomputed over the six stated minor ages alone, with the full-ladder value beside it.
